sections.h2: Who handles a Lawrence County tax bill
sections.html:
Four offices in Louisa handle the tax year between them, and the PVA and the sheriff share the same Main Cross Street address. Each covers its own step.

  • Property Valuation Administrator (PVA): 122 Main Cross Street, Louisa, KY 41230. The PVA sets the assessed value and takes homestead applications.
  • Sheriff: 122 Main Cross Street, Louisa. Phone (606) 638-4368. The sheriff takes payment.
  • County Clerk: runs the appeals board paperwork and, after April, the sale of unpaid bills. The clerk's site posts the current delinquent list.
  • County Attorney: mails the warning letters to owners whose bills have moved to the clerk.

Taxing districts set different rates, so the sheriff's bill and the PVA's assessment for your own parcel are the figures that count.

sections.h2: Lawrence County housing at a glance
sections.html: Louisa is the lone city and holds the courthouse. The county had an estimated 15,765 residents in July 2025, down from 16,293 in 2020, spread over about 416 square miles. It holds 7,737 housing units and 6,342 households, with 77.8 percent owned by their occupants. The middle home value is $111,700. Typical owner costs run $1,216 a month for mortgaged homes and $386 for paid-off ones, and typical rent is $760. At these price levels, an unpaid bill can eat a noticeable share of the sale, so know your payoff early. Alcohol sales are limited to Louisa city limits.

KRS 134.015 sets the year-end deadline at December 31 and gives a 2 percent discount to anyone who clears the whole bill by November 1. January costs 5 percent extra, and February onward costs 10 percent plus a sheriff's add-on fee, so a bill paid on February 1 or later runs roughly a fifth higher before any commission.

Late-mailed bills fall under a state alternative schedule that allows 30 days per stage. Oil and gas bills also exist in Lawrence County. The clerk's sale leaves out the 2023 oil and gas bills, so ask the sheriff whether one is attached to your parcel.

The sequence runs in order. Step one is a sit-down with the PVA's staff. Step two is the May viewing window for the roll. Step three is the written appeal, which the clerk must have by the next workday after viewing ends. Step four is a hearing before the local board about a month later. Only evidence counts at the hearing, so bring proof such as a description of the lot and buildings, insurance papers, construction costs and listings of nearby sales.

Written reasons follow any change the board makes. Hearings may be recorded, and a paid representative has to fit the categories in KRS 133.120. Skipping the board closes off the Kentucky Claims Commission.

Eligible owners are those who have turned 65 and those classified as fully disabled. The 2025-26 deduction is $49,100 off the assessed value. About 19.9 percent of local residents are past 65, so many sellers here may already have it on file.

The PVA's courthouse office takes the form. A claim built on disability has to be renewed each year. Two groups are excused from renewing: owners whose disability is service-connected, and people Social Security or a state retirement system has ruled permanently and totally disabled. Ask the PVA what happens to the exemption once the house sells.

sections.h2: How the clerk sells unpaid tax bills
sections.html:
Anything the sheriff has not collected by April 15 becomes a certificate of delinquency at the clerk's office, with interest of 1 percent a month. Letters from the county attorney go out, and the clerk publishes the list before the sale date. At the sale a registered outside buyer can buy the lien, and from then on the owner pays that buyer. The clerk's draft-style sale rules also tell an owner how much a buyer may be paying.

Lawrence County Clerk delinquent tax sale rules
Sale stepRule
RegistrationAt least 10 business days before the sale
Deposit$10 per bill, capped at $250, not refundable
Prior year certificatesSeparate list due 10 business days before the sale
Bidders per entityOne potential purchaser
Order of purchaseRandom drawing, lowest number picks first, in rounds
PaymentCash, certified check, money order or company check
RefundsNone after the sale

The lien on the land from delinquent taxes lasts eleven years under KRS 134.015, no matter who owns the property.

sections.h2: Before you list a Lawrence County house
sections.html:
• Ask the sheriff at (606) 638-4368 for the current bill and any earlier unpaid year.
  • Look through the clerk's delinquent list for any certificate tied to the parcel.
  • If you have the homestead exemption, find out from the PVA what becomes of it after a sale.
  • Compare your assessment with the sales of similar houses before the May inspection window opens, in case a dispute is worth filing.
  • Agree on the split of the current bill in the sales contract.
  • Because the PVA and the sheriff share one Main Cross Street address, one trip to Louisa can settle both the assessment question and the bill itself.
  • Ask whether any oil and gas bill is attached to the parcel.

Owners who want no repairs or showings can request a direct cash offer. Any tax still due is paid from the sale money at closing regardless of buyer.

The assessment is made as of January 1, so the bill follows whoever owned the parcel on that date. If you sell in the spring, the bill that arrives in the fall may still carry your name. Put the split in the sales contract, and the closing agent will prorate the year on the settlement statement and send the sheriff its share from the proceeds.

A cash sale skips the buyer's lender and its separate tax search, which removes one common cause of delay. The payoff figures still have to be right, so request them from the sheriff and the clerk a few days before the closing date.

sections.h2: What a payoff request should include
sections.html:
When you call the sheriff for a payoff, give the parcel and the owner name exactly as they appear on the deed. Ask for the current-year amount, any earlier year still open, and the date through which the figure holds. Then repeat the same request at the clerk's office to see whether any certificate exists. Write down who you spoke to and when, and ask for the numbers in writing if you can.

Hand both figures to the title company before you sign a sales contract. The company deducts what is owed from your proceeds at closing and pays the offices directly, so you do not need to carry a check to Louisa yourself. If a bill has already reached the clerk, the lien follows the land, so it must be cleared whichever buyer you choose.

faqs.q: Where is the Lawrence County tax bill paid?
faqs.a: The Lawrence County Sheriff collects it at 122 Main Cross Street in Louisa. Call (606) 638-4368 to confirm the amount and the payment methods before you go.

faqs.q: How much does paying early save in Lawrence County?
faqs.a: Two percent comes off a bill paid in full by November 1, and the full printed amount is owed from November 2 to December 31 under KRS 134.015.

faqs.q: What comes first when disputing a value here?
faqs.a: A conference at the PVA's office. Without it the board that reviews assessments will not take the appeal.

faqs.q: How big is the homestead exemption?
faqs.a: It is $49,100 for 2025-26. The owner has to be at least 65 or classified as fully disabled, and the form goes to the PVA.

faqs.q: Can an outside buyer purchase an unpaid bill here?
faqs.a: Yes, when the certificate stays unpaid until the clerk's sale. A registered purchaser can buy the lien, and the owner then settles with that purchaser.
